extracted.intended_audience: evolutionary psychologists, humor researchers, social scientists, and students interested in sexual selection and human mating behavior
extracted.subtask_description: Operationalize and evaluate humor as a fitness-indicating signal in mate choice: includes measurable predictions (intelligence → humor → mating success), how humor ability was measured, contextual functions, and status-dependent effects of humor style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligence predicts humor ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Both general and verbal intelligence correlate with rated funniness of generated material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Greengross & Miller (2011) intelligence was measured with Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices (general) and a vocabulary subtest (verbal); humor ability was rated based on participants' written cartoon captions. Use objective psychometric tests of intelligence and independent ratings of produced humor to test this link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor ability predicts mating success
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor production ability correlates with self-reported mating success (e.g., lifetime number of sexual partners), controlling for other variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure mating success with standard self-report metrics and include covariates; analyze whether rated funniness of produced material predicts mating outcomes above and beyond control variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex difference in humor production (males higher)
rubrics_metrics.description: Males show higher mean humor production ability than females, consistent with sexual selection where one sex competes more intensely on cognitive-fitness signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect higher mean scores for male participants on production tasks; interpret differences in light of display/chooser roles in mating contexts rather than global incapacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness indicator: costly to fake
rubrics_metrics.description: To function as a fitness indicator, the trait must be costly or hard-to-fake — you can't convincingly pretend to have it on cue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the humor ability requires genuine cognitive resources and spontaneous creativity rather than rote or memorized lines; signals that are easy to fake weaken the indicator interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness indicator: reliably correlates with general cognitive ability
rubrics_metrics.description: The trait should reliably correlate with general cognitive ability (i.e., taps the same underlying machinery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate empirical correlations between humor production measures and established cognitive tests to support the fitness-indicator claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness indicator: attractive across cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: The trait should be attractive across cultures (though weighted differently).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect cross-cultural evidence or show that humor-related preferences appear broadly in mate-choice self-reports to bolster the universality claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness indicator: prized in conversation when assessing mates
rubrics_metrics.description: The trait should be prized in casual mate-assessment contexts (people report sense of humor as a desirable trait).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey data on mate preferences and naturalistic observations of conversational contexts to show that humor matters in real-world mate choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational definition of humor ability (production-focused)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor ability measured as capacity to generate captions/responses that other people find funny, produced quickly/on demand and across diverse prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish production ability from appreciation (laughing at jokes) and use tasks that require spontaneous generation across varied prompts; have independent raters judge funniness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production vs. appreciation asymmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a sex-differentiated asymmetry: men produce more humor (displayers), women appreciate more selectively (choosers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating humor in mating contexts, consider who is initiating humor versus who is evaluating it; measure initiation frequency and selective responses, not just laugh rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function: humor as mate signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor functions as a display of cognitive fitness used in sexual selection (signaling intelligence to potential mates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret funny production in mating contexts as potentially costly signaling; test links to mating outcomes and cognitive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function: same-sex status competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor serves in same-sex status competitions (wit duels to gain hierarchical position among rivals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine contexts of rivalry and status negotiation; evaluate humor performance and its social consequences for status within same-sex groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function: tension reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor reduces tension and defuses potential conflict in close groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider affiliative and conciliatory uses of humor; measure effects on group cohesion and tension in observational or experimental settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function: coalition formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Shared laughter and humorous exchanges bind allies and help form coalitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess mutual laughter and in-group humor as predictors of alliance strength and cooperative behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function: cognitive coordination (testing shared minds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor tests whether others 'get it,' revealing shared mental architecture and mutual understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use humor that requires perspective-taking or shared knowledge to probe cognitive alignment between interlocutors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-deprecating vs. other-deprecating humor: status-dependent attractiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-deprecating humor by high-status men is attractive (signals security); self-deprecation by low-status men is unattractive (signals weakness). Other-deprecating humor is generally less attractive than self-deprecating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing the attractiveness of humor styles, consider the producer's status: the same humor tactic can have opposite effects depending on status and audience interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the humor demonstrate cognitive complexity?
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic criterion: does the humor require cognitive effort that signals intelligence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate semantic complexity, novelty, ambiguity-resolution, wordplay, or conceptual combination that indicate mental effort rather than mere repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the humor produced spontaneously or rehearsed?
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic criterion: spontaneous production is more impressive (and a stronger signal) than rehearsed material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate improvised responses from memorized jokes in measurement tasks; spontaneity strengthens the inference of underlying ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the producer in a signaling-relevant context?
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic criterion: does the producer face an audience/context where signaling matters (mate choice, status competition, in-group bonding)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret humorous displays differently depending on social context; prioritize contexts where selection pressures plausibly operate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the producer's status appropriate for chosen humor type?
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic criterion: does the type of humor (self- vs other-deprecating) fit the producer's social position?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess audience perceptions of status congruence and whether humor tactics are costly or beneficial given the producer's sociosexual standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement model: recommended variables and operational measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical model includes general intelligence (Raven's APM), verbal intelligence (vocabulary), humor production ability (rated funniness of generated cartoon captions), and mating success (lifetime number of sexual partners, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use validated psychometric instruments for intelligence, standardized production tasks for humor (diverse prompts, time-limited), independent funniness ratings, and clear mating-success measures; control for confounds in analyses.
